subject: Tenant egress fencing + standby warmup checklist / AcroBank private VPC
messages:
From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
To: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@acrobank.com>, corp-netops@acrobank.com
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-07-09T08:12:00Z
Subject: Tenant egress fencing + standby warmup checklist / AcroBank private VPC

Hi Elena / NetOps team,

Following our scope call last week, we pulled together a concise checklist to validate tenant-level egress zoning for your EU private VPC and the APAC cold->warm standby sequence. Goal: confirm there are no unexpected egress paths during failover and that the standby cluster in APAC can warm within the RTO window without cross-border data egress.

High-level asks for your team before the dry-run:
- Confirm advertised prefixes and permitted egress CIDR list for each tenant (we need an authoritative table).
- Confirm whether NAT/proxy for tenant egress is regional (per-tenant NAT) or centralized in the EU control plane.
- Provide any outbound 3rd-party endpoints that must remain EU-only (SaaS vendors, telemetry endpoints).
- Approve routing policy for standby warmup: allow internal controlplane-only peering for cache pre-warm, block public egress until cutover authorization.

Attached: egress_fencing_matrix.xlsx (tenant-level CIDR / allowed destinations) and a draft standby-warmup-runbook.

Can Marissa and Karthik confirm we have the right gating checks on our side (RBAC, KMS locality checks, pre-warm KV policies)?

Thanks,
Aditya

-- 
Aditya Rao
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Date: 2028-07-09T14:33:00Z
Subject: Re: Tenant egress fencing + standby warmup checklist / AcroBank private VPC

Thanks Aditya — useful start. A few clarifications from NetOps side:

1) Advertised prefixes: we maintain a per-tenant outbound allowlist; I'll attach the current export. Note that some tenants use a managed SaaS aggregator in the EU (analytics-pool.eu.example.com) which must not be routed via APAC.
2) NAT topology: currently we have centralized egress NAT in each region. For EU it's regional and restricted to EU egress IPs.
3) Standby warmup: we need to ensure that the KV cache pre-warm traffic for anonymized models doesn't hit any external SaaS. Can Redwood pre-warm using internal-only endpoints?

Open question: during warmup we expect significant cross-region controlplane chatter for orchestration. What minimal controlplane APIs would cause user data to transit outside the EU boundary? We need the list so we can run DPI checks.

I'll upload our allowlist and a short NetOps note to the shared Drive.

Best,
Elena

--
Elena Rossi
Head of Cloud Networking, AcroBank

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@acrobank.com>
Date: 2028-07-10T09:18:00Z
Subject: Re: Tenant egress fencing + standby warmup checklist / AcroBank private VPC

Folks — quick technical notes from the residency/runbook team:

- Controlplane traffic: metadata only (model/version selectors, rollout signals, health pings). No inference payloads should be in controlplane APIs. Runtime token exchange and attestation material are ephemeral; we will add an explicit DPI signature to the call to show there is no payload leakage.
- Pre-warm approach: we propose two modes (A/B):
  A) Internal-only pre-warm: run synthetic prompts against a locally-isolated stub model that exercises KV cache and sequence length distributions — no customer PII or external callbacks. This is our default for EU-bound tenants.
  B) Full-model pre-warm (optional): requires signed authorization from NetOps; will be limited to internal tunnels and blocked from public egress by default.
- Routing policy: Redwood will implement a short-lived route-blacklist during standby warmup to block known public SaaS endpoints you identify in the allowlist attached.

Action items for Redwood:
- Karthik: add KMS locality validation step to the warmup checklist (reject warm if keys cannot be validated as EU-resident).
- Marissa: produce a pre-warm telemetry packet showing controlplane-only calls and expected byte counts (for your DPI tests).

Hannah

From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
To: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@acrobank.com>, corp-netops@acrobank.com
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-07-10T16:42:00Z
Subject: Re: Tenant egress fencing + standby warmup checklist / AcroBank private VPC

Thanks Elena and Hannah — taking these items into the runbook iteration. Draft checklist below (for sign-off prior to the DR dry-run):

1) Authorization
- NetOps signed allowlist received and attached to ticket.
- AcroBank approves internal-only pre-warm mode A (default).

2) Network gating (pre-cutover)
- Apply temporary outbound ACL on standby to block public SaaS endpoints (per acrobank-tenant-allowlist.csv).
- Confirm advertised prefixes: attached matrix must reconcile (NetOps -> Redwood).

3) Cryptographic locality check
- Karthik to validate KMS key metadata locally; fail warmup if keys indicate non-EU residency.

4) Telemetry/DPI validation
- Marissa to push a 15-minute telemetry extract showing controlplane-only flows for Redwood pre-warm window.

5) Fail-safe posture
- If any unauthorized egress detected during warmup, automatically abort warmup and revert routing.
- Post-mortem within 4 hours with packet captures and controlplane logs.

6) Cutover authorization
- Warmup complete -> NetOps confirm zero external egress -> formal cutover window opens.

If this looks OK I will add explicit CLI commands and the small sanity-automation that flips ACLs and runs the KMS check. I expect to push an updated runbook and the automation snippet to the shared Drive by EOD.

Next steps: Elena / NetOps please confirm sign-off on items 1 and 2; Karthik / Marissa please confirm you have the runbook items.

Cheers,
Aditya
